adopted: The fail=true MUST wins: the discharge completes whatever the register says, because the artifact states it without qualification and a controller whose rollback arrives after the id was retired is exactly the case the sentence exists for.
consequences: txn-discharge-unknown-id-refused pins the unflagged case only; nothing in the corpus carries fail=true with an unknown id, so no vector currently distinguishes the readings.
The two readings differ observably: one admits the discharge and one refuses it with amqp:transaction:unknown-id, which is a verdict a vector could pin the moment the reading is chosen.
evidence: The transaction machine completes it without consulting the register, because the artifact states the completion unconditionally: the coordinator MUST always be able to complete a discharge whose fail flag is set to true.
question: What happens when both readings apply — a fail=true discharge naming an id that was never allocated, or one already discharged.
